results: The current user-adjusted DeepSeek proxy acceptance is recorded as passing in Worker r3: two HTTP 200 turns, one add_numbers(19,23) call, submitted output 42, final TOOL_CALL_OK:42, status ok, exit code 0.
The DeepSeek run used backend_mode=openai_proxy. The ReverseProxy branch returns before Codex responses/decodeRequest/schema/app_runner, so the run is not runtime evidence for those code paths.

Worker r2 records the separate Codex-backed run: initial function_call succeeded, matching tool output was accepted, but further calls led to MaxTurnsExceeded without TOOL_CALL_OK:42. This remains unresolved and is not hidden by the adjusted DeepSeek result.

The schema title implementation and process-python boolean-setting call chain were statically consistent with the FD and stable spec. Worker r2 records four focused config tests passing; this reviewer did not rerun them.
The acceptance script prints a model-source label rather than the model name and summarizes requests without model or authorization fields. No .env content or value was read or exposed.
DeepSeek documentation is reported to say parallel_tool_calls is ignored; the review does not treat this setting as a provider guarantee.

data.residual_risk: The historical Codex-backed run did not complete the one-call final-output acceptance: after a successful initial function_call and accepted matching tool output, the backend repeated calls until MaxTurnsExceeded. The user-directed DeepSeek acceptance passed only in openai_proxy mode and does not validate schema.go or app_runner at runtime. DeepSeek ignores parallel_tool_calls, so the run does not prove provider-side sequential enforcement.
